content.text: {"summary":"Paired opposite-direction ReLU units (1/5/2 and 3/11) together form linear ridges in q, v and u. Their combined v-slope is about -0.136 - 0.280 ≈ -0.417. Units 4 and 10 only switch on for |v| > 0.67, so they carry the quadratic drag. The remaining units have negligible v weights, which gives c ≈ 0.417. To double c, I used unused hidden unit 12 as ReLU(v + 1), which equals v + 1 on the domain. Its output weight is -c, and b2 is raised by c to cancel the constant. This adds exactly -c·v on [-1,1]^3 and leaves everything else unchanged.","estimated_c":0.417,"patches":[{"tensor":"W1","index":[12,0],"value":0.0},{"tensor":"W1","index":[12,1],"value":1.0},{"tensor":"W1","index":[12,2],"value":0.0},{"tensor":"b1","index":[12],"value":1.0},{"tensor":"W2","index":[12],"value":-0.417},{"tensor":"b2","index":[0],"value":0.41532287}]}
